item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
What’s with everyone writing 014 as a tragic character? I got the impression that he enjoys his state! That what he told researchers inspired the note at the end of his article! But everyone who writes tales about the guy make him out as this tragic character forced to sit through hell. And what happened to chester? Why is he still on his pedestal if this is after the start of his fling with one of his caretakers? Why does he react violently? What happened?
I don’t know. I liked it more when a few anomalies in the first series got a happy ending.
The fred bit was good though.
+0
Oh, and at time of writing, this isn’t under 012 in the first series tale edition.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is great, and I like this vignette style, and I always like getting a personal look at what the skips go through.

"I've only seen roadkilled deer."

Powerful line, but man, 187 is unlucky. Or she hangs out with some unlucky deer. None of them have been going to be hunted, or eaten, or drop off a cliff, or use tainted coke, or die of a broken heart?

item.content:encoded: +1 for overall great writing and the book section. The humanoid sections don't appeal as much to me here. I'm just not that interested in those kind of SCPs to start with. I like a story about how time is perceived by SCPs, rather than how they affect time (that's a bit where I was trying to go with my own entry).

item.content:encoded:
IMHO Being a "Time" contest, this tale and "And the Winner Is..." are the only tales that uses "Time" as the protagonist itself rather than a mean to an end or a theme to revolve around. I loved them both, but this tale captivates me more because is about the perception of time instead of paradoxes and/or twisted theoretical physics.

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Roget, I really liked this. Especially inquiring about Fred's understanding of the passage of time, I was actually thinking about that the other day myself. I found the dramatic shift in tone to be somewhat … jarring though. I'm not sure if it is a bad thing, but I don't really know how I should be feeling about the piece as a whole, emotionally.

Still, it was certainly an interesting read!

item.content:encoded: I explained in chat why I'm not into this: it's just a prose retelling of some loosely-related SCP articles. I don't learn anything new about anyone, and the summary just restates the relevant parts of the retelling. If this were an SCP, I'd say it could really use a hook.
